findings.text: `int(nth)` silently truncates or wraps large values before the bounds check. For example, `Nth(s, uint64(math.MaxUint64))` becomes -1 and returns the last element instead of an out-of-bounds error. On 32-bit platforms, `int64(1<<32)` becomes 0 and returns the first element.

raw:
Conversion int(nth) can overflow/truncate for large uint64 or int64 on 32-bit: e.g. uint64(1<<32) -> int 0 on 32-bit, or uint64 max -> -1 returns last element instead of error.
